analysis.title: Assessing AI risks (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: UBS views AI as a significant structural opportunity. It says NVIDIA's results and those of other key AI-related companies point to robust underlying demand for AI compute capacity, which remains in tight supply.

UBS expects aggregate AI capital spending to rise from USD 1tr this year to USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. Growing advance orders for compute capacity should support faster cloud revenue growth, and consumer AI agent adoption should underpin the next phase of AI demand.

Investors are increasingly focused on whether AI spending can generate sustainable profits, given higher financing costs. UBS does not think recent tech volatility derails the investment case, but says the AI trade is becoming more sensitive to geopolitical and macro developments.

Monetization is the ultimate test. With nearly USD 3tr expected to be deployed over two years, AI revenue must scale into profits and cash flows to justify the spending. Cloud revenue growth has been encouraging, but investors want evidence of monetization across the value chain, including business models disrupted by AI.
UBS expects greater dispersion in company performance because of intense competition at both the intelligence and application layers.

The US tightened AI chip export restrictions this week with new rules limiting China's and other US adversaries' access to offshore computing power that uses American-designed processors. Enforcement is uncertain. UBS thinks the revenue impact for US chipmakers and hyperscalers should be limited because GPU and cloud capacity is already constrained.
The new chip restrictions could add pressure to consensus 2028 AI capex estimates, which are considerably higher than UBS's. Downward revisions to capex estimates could lead to market volatility.
Greater Democratic control of US state governments after the midterms could generate headlines about state and local restrictions on the AI buildout, weighing on sentiment.

UBS's base case is relatively modest Fed tightening over the next 12 months. The latest inflation data raises the risk that the Fed shifts from gradual quarterly hikes to consecutive 25-basis-point moves. Financial stress has already emerged among more leveraged infrastructure providers.

Positioning advice: stay engaged with structural AI but with more selectivity, broader diversification and less concentrated exposure. UBS favors financially strong established tech platforms and semiconductor and hardware companies with durable competitive advantages. Defensive tech can complement cyclical AI holdings, and exposure to other sectors and regions adds resilience.

NVIDIA reported third-quarter profit and revenue beats on Tuesday and guided fiscal fourth-quarter revenue to about USD 130bn, above Wall Street estimates. It raised next fiscal year revenue growth guidance to 75% from a previous 70%. Shares rose 4.9% after hours after a 0.4% fall on Tuesday.
The Nasdaq closed 0.7% lower on Tuesday, before the NVIDIA results, on concerns over chip demand and the sustainability of AI capex.

tension_points.bull_case: NVIDIA's results and those of other key AI companies point to robust demand for AI compute in tight supply. Advance orders for compute are growing and should accelerate cloud revenue growth. Consumer AI agent adoption underpins the next phase. UBS forecasts capex rising from USD 1tr to USD 1.5tr by 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Investors question whether the buildout of nearly USD 3tr over two years can produce sustainable profits amid higher financing costs. Leveraged infrastructure providers already show financial stress, and the new chip export rules could pull down 2028 capex estimates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Downward revisions to consensus 2028 AI capex estimates, or a shift from gradual quarterly Fed hikes to consecutive 25-basis-point hikes, would pressure the bull case.
